headline: A 2018 executive order sets up a federal council of agencies focused on crime prevention and helping people return to society after prison.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order creates a Federal Interagency Council on Crime Prevention and Improving Reentry. The council brings together several federal agencies to work on preventing crime and on "reentry," meaning the return of people to their communities after time in prison or jail. No summary was provided, so the council's exact members, duties, and powers are not described here.

who_it_affects.how: Agencies named to the council would coordinate their work on crime prevention and reentry.
The council's work is aimed at improving reentry, though the title alone does not say what specific programs or services may change.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed March 7, 2018; executive orders usually take effect when signed.
